executive_assessment.text: Named local depth differentiates urban rainfall, heat and drought classifications from historical wildfire-poverty overlap in Şanlıurfa and Mardin.

Refugee-host service, employment and cohesion evidence is retained with undated-population and project-design limits. The review did not establish a climate-conflict or reverse insecurity-to-adaptation pathway.

Seven named basins and Ceyhan have planned flood/drought capacity investments, while Samsun, Sakarya, Muğla and Konya have reported local-plan outputs. Planned reach and published plans do not prove reduced vulnerability.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024 reports: The strategy rates urban heavy-precipitation risk at its highest level in Mersin, Adana, Hatay, Osmaniye, Samsun, Ordu, Kayseri, Kahramanmaraş, Şırnak, Batman and Diyarbakır.

Source dated 2024 reports: The strategy highlights Antalya, Mersin, Istanbul, Bursa and Izmir for urban heatwave risk, citing sprawl, impermeable surfaces, constrained streams and limited green space.
Source dated 2024 reports: The water-resources assessment identifies high current drought risk in Konya, Isparta, Aksaray, Niğde, Nevşehir, the eastern Mediterranean and all Southeastern Anatolia.

Source dated 2022-06 reports: The CCDR identifies Şanlıurfa and Mardin as wildfire and socioeconomic-vulnerability hotspots; their annual land-burned shares averaged 6.6% and 5.4% in 2011–2021, and about one-fifth of Türkiye’s poor lived in high wildfire-risk areas.

Source dated 2024-06-27 reports: At June 2024 approval, the project planned flood-control works and nature-based solutions across seven named basins, with over 150,000 people targeted for direct benefit.
Source dated 2024-06-27 reports: The approval plan included real-time agricultural drought monitoring in the Ceyhan Basin and monitoring data for 10,000 farmers to support water-stress decisions.

Source dated 2025-10-03 reports: At project close in October 2025, the programme reported 2025–2030 local adaptation plans and sectoral vulnerability/risk analyses for Samsun, Sakarya, Muğla and Konya, plus urban climate-finance strategies.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 14 of 14 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

No inspected source directly links climate hazards or adaptation to violent conflict in Türkiye. UNDP documents refugee-host social cohesion, public-service and employment pressures separately from climate risks; these are not joined into a climate-conflict pathway.

No inspected primary source documents conflict or insecurity blocking adaptation implementation or climate-service access. The regional UNHCR 3RP 2025 PDF could not be opened and was not used as country evidence.
The ministry strategy provides named city/province risks, but its cited local results do not specify the scenario or period; its urban study cautions against extrapolating results to entire cities.
The UNDP refugee population figures have no reference date on the page and should not be used as a current baseline; the project is marked completed in January 2025 without an outcome evaluation.

World Bank flood/drought and forest project announcements report planned areas, targets and intended capacities. No later project-status evidence was used to establish 2026 implementation or results; the wildfire project’s 14 provinces are unnamed in its release.

The ministry strategy PDF could not be reopened in the current browser attempt and a repeat download reset; the claims rely on a prior direct full-document extraction and reading, not search-indexed excerpts.
The return-period flood simulation has no future calendar horizon and is excluded under the bank's projected-evidence contract; the original claim remains in the extraction audit.
Refugee-host service and employment tensions remain separate contextual evidence. They are not joined to climate hazards, and migration/refugee status is not treated as a threat characteristic.
The ministry's local rankings have incomplete scenario, period and infrastructure detail; they are selected screening findings, not complete city-level or current household risk estimates.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
